      <title>Ukraine confirms it used naval drones to strike two Russian ships off Libya</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/ukraine-naval-drones-strike-russian-warship-libya</link>
      <description><p>Ukraine’s security service says seven drones were launched from mothership in operation that sank Merkury warship</p><p>Ukraine has confirmed it deployed naval drones in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya</a> on Sunday, including one that sank the corvette Merkury, one of Russia’s newest vessels.</p><p>Ukraine’s security service, the SBU, said seven domestically made naval drones were launched from a mothership in the operation, which Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as “exemplary”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/ukraine-naval-drones-strike-russian-warship-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya</link>
      <description><p>No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia</p><p>A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.</p><p>The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits</p><p>Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.</p><p>The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover.       <description><p>Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds</p><p>One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.</p><p>In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament.       <description><p>Carney watches on as comedian lampoons US leader and his interest in men’s backsides at correspondents’ event Ottawa</p><p>Canada’s prime minister, Mark Carney, was joined on stage in Ottawa by a Donald Trump impersonator who mocked the US president to raucous laughter from a crowd of politicians and journalists at a parliamentary press gallery dinner on Saturday.</p><p>With coiffed hair and an ill-fitting suit, comedian Mark Critch – who portrays the president on the sketch show This Hour Has 22 Minutes – danced on to the stage and lampooned the trade war Trump started as well as the president’s threats to annex Canada.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/23/canada-trump-impersonator-press-dinner">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Island’s labour minister, Colin Jordan, says agreement acknowledges links between Speightstown and UK city are rooted in slave trade</p><p>A town in Barbados known as “Little Bristol” has signed a “twinning’” agreement with the UK city, marking a new chapter in a centuries-long relationship rooted in the transatlantic slave trade.</p><p>Barbados says the new partnership between Speightstown and Bristol is part of its wider push for reparatory justice, built in small steps rather than around a multi-trillion-pound claim.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/23/barbados-minister-speightstown-bristol-deal-slave-trade-reparations">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba</link>
      <description><p>New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people</p><p>• <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/ng-interactive/2026/sep/16/slave-trade-wealth-britain-financial-system-bank-of-england-enslaved-africans">Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds</a></p><p>British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.</p><p>Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/nov/24/labor-penny-wong-us-china-anthony-albanese-final-sitting-week-ntwnfb</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">breaking news email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>The government will save more than it spends, says <strong>Jim Chalmers</strong>, but it won’t be a “slash and burn” budget update.</p><p>Unlike the federal budget, where we get plenty of notice of when it will be handed down, the government only gives us a few days notice for the mid-financial year economic and fiscal outlook (or Myefo).</p><p>There’s still a fair bit of work to do to finalise it all, but we’ve made enough progress to be confident that at this stage there will be a modest net save in the budget.</p><p>We’re not going to slash and burn in the budget where that would impact the payments that people receive or where it would impact some of the more sensitive parts of the economy. But we haven’t focused the savings on just one portfolio. There will be a number of savings in the mid-year update. They will be substantial, as I said. These are serious times.</p><p>You can see in the quite extraordinary reaction on the stock market just how volatile global markets are right now.       <description><p>Temporary quotas on vehicles entering the bloc tariff-free will also apply to cars from the UK, Japan and Turkey</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/24/jensen-huang-nvidia-stock-markets-ai-trade-us-political-backlash-donald-trump-latest-news-updates">Business live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p></p><p>The EU will next month impose its threatened caps on the number of Chinese hybrid cars that can be imported into the bloc without facing a tariff, the European Commission has announced.</p><p>The quotas will also apply to hybrids from Japan, Turkey, South Korea and the UK, but the principal purpose is to limit imports from China after <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/09/china-agrees-to-curb-hybrid-car-exports-to-eu-in-landmark-deal">an agreement with Beijing in October</a> that has led to a rise in exports to the bloc.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/24/eu-cap-chinese-hybrid-ev-imports-tariff-uk">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/24/ebikes-screens-and-failing-manners-pose-challenge-for-dutch-cycling-culture</link>
      <description><p>Awareness campaign reminds public ‘traffic is a team sport’ amid less civility and more collisions on roads</p><p>For decades the Netherlands has been famed for its proud cycling culture, with a network of 23,000 miles of bike paths used by everyone from children under eight to adults over 80.</p><p>In recent years, however, like so many countries around the world, it has seen a dramatic change in the type of vehicles using those lanes: no longer the preserve of pedal bikes, they are used by all manner of two-wheeled vehicles including electric cargo bikes, thick-tyred “fatbikes”, speed pedelecs, electric scooters and even some micro cars.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/24/ebikes-screens-and-failing-manners-pose-challenge-for-dutch-cycling-culture">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/23/andy-burnham-brexit-deal-eu</link>
      <description><p>Prime minister also says former Tory premiers who have criticised revival of Brexit debate are ‘stuck in the past’</p><p>Andy Burnham has said it would be “unthinkable” for the UK to rejoin the EU without holding another referendum, offering his strongest commitment yet to directly consulting the public if he concludes Britain should go back in.</p><p>The prime minister is planning to set out the long-term options for closer ties with the bloc next month, with concrete steps coming after the next general election, as he has pledged to stick to Labour’s manifesto red lines.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/23/andy-burnham-brexit-deal-eu">Continue reading...</a></description>

France will seek European-level sanctions against Iran in response to cyberattacks on hundreds of supermarket fridges, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Tuesday, after accusing Tehran's Revolutionary Guards of orchestrating the October sabotage. Iran's foreign ministry said the accusations were "baseless and one-sided".

While the extension of France’s health pass and other new anti-Covid 19 measures announced by President Emmanuel Macron Monday night are yet to be hammered out in detail, what’s certain is that a full-throttled return to a normal life of frequenting café terraces, restaurants, cinemas, theatres and other culture and leisure activities will now hinge on having a pass sanitaire (or health pass).

rumours</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261110-macrons-file-new-defamation-lawsuit-against-us-podcaster-over-transgender-rumours</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte filed a second lawsuit against US right-wing podcaster Candace Owens over false claims on her gender, accusing her of continuing to spread the allegations and profiting from them despite earlier legal action. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">efe09190-dcbf-11f1-9487-5f60e87d1ec6</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 04:33:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg">© Abdul Saboor, POOL/AFP/File</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Top contemporary French artist Christian Boltanski dies aged 76</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210714-top-contemporary-french-artist-christian-boltanski-dies-aged-76</link><description>
Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7135ce8-e4c8-11eb-89be-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 18:44:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg">© Miguel Riopa, AFP</source><dc:creator>NEWS WIRES</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Crumbs': French PM's 1.6% minimum wage increase fails to placate unions</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-french-pm-lecornu-announces-increase-minimum-wage-bid-to-calm-protests</link><description>
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f6ee1d4e-dc43-11f1-9280-633626f68692</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:52:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Paris police officers go on trial over 2020 beating of Black man</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-paris-police-officers-go-on-trial-over-2020-beating-of-black-man</link><description>
Three French police officers went on trial Monday over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">476e3e4a-dc24-11f1-9f04-f3d8b2b0702c</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:08:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg">© Thomas Samson, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students vow to continue protests despite concessions from Macron govt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261026-macron-vows-concrete-measures-to-address-student-demands-after-unrest</link><description>
French student leaders on Monday called for more protests despite President Emmanuel Macron's pledge of  "concrete and strong" measures to address their demands after weeks of nationwide unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met with high school representatives alongside education ministers to announce follow-up action ranging from a total overhaul of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup to a cap on class sizes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ade564d2-d134-11f1-9bc8-6d20ccb9a352</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 12:25:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>How the French army trains for 'high-intensity' combat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20210714-how-the-french-army-trains-for-high-intensity-conflict</link><description>
France's new military programming law increases the country's defence budget to 2 percent of GDP by 2025. It's an investment in the modernisation of equipment, but also in the training of soldiers. The aim is to teach soldiers to face an army at least as well equipped as that of France in a context of global rearmament. Our reporters Fadile Bhayat, Mandi Heshmati and Caroline Grandjean followed French troops during a "high-intensity" training exercise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">023ce07e-e41d-11eb-a94a-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 14:42:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Fadile BHAYAT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says 'racist terrorist attack’ in Trappes marks turning point for France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261023-french-prosecutors-investigate-paris-shooting-as-suspected-terror-attack</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron described Friday’s drive-by shooting in the western suburb of Trappes as a “terrorist and racist attack”, saying it marks a turning point for France. One person was killed and at least four people, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded in the shooting, apparently at random. Two of the victims have immigrant backgrounds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">72670cfa-ced0-11f1-8bc7-bb90dbb6a8a1</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:08:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg">© Hannah McKay, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>'A lot of French politicians are out of touch with a large part of the population'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20220209-a-lot-of-french-politicians-are-out-of-touch-with-a-large-part-of-the-population</link><description>
Our guest is Fabien Truong, a sociologist, author and associate professor at the University of Paris. A former schoolteacher, he spent a decade following the lives of around 20 of his students, charting their progress from the time they took their end of school exams to when they finished their higher education. Those 10 years took in the riots that rocked France back in 2005 to the terror attacks of January 2015. He gives us his take on the French presidential election campaign, as seen from the suburbs.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2534ffb8-8980-11ec-8ce4-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 12:31:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sharon GAFFNEY</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says world leaders have made 'stupid' comments on France riots based on fake AI videos</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261021-macron-says-world-leaders-have-made-stupid-comments-on-france-riots-based-on-fake-ai-videos</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron took aim at world leaders including US President Donald Trump for trying to exploit the riots and looting that broke out alongside peaceful demonstrations in France Saturday for their own political advantage. Another wave of demonstrations against France's worsening cost of living is planned for the coming Saturday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2c665312-cd42-11f1-8dbc-290623bfb92e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:48:11 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg">© Benoit Tessier, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Tefal campaign': with Covid-19 monopolising voters' minds, nothing sticks</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20220209-tefal-campaign-pandemic-prudent-president-keep-french-election-race-on-the-backburner</link><description>
Presidential campaigns offer an abundance of catch phrases, whether slogans finessed by a candidate's team to deliver maximum impact or coined spontaneously on the trail. The proclamations – and gaffes – of presidential hopefuls bring texture to an election race and come to define a campaign, whether for a news cycle or forever in the history books. FRANCE 24 brings you the buzzwords of the 2022 French presidential race. In the spotlight: "Tefal campaign".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f4e47fa4-88f4-11ec-97bf-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 10:43:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png">© FMM Graphic Studio</source><dc:creator>Tracy MCNICOLL</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Teen wounds headmaster and teacher after opening fire at French school</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-french-police-arrest-14-year-old-after-two-teaching-staff-wounded-by-hunting-rifle-fire</link><description>
Two teaching staff were shot and wounded by a 14-year-old boy armed with a hunting rifle at a school in Aubagne near Marseille Monday morning, French Education Minister ‌Édouard Geffray said. Authorities said the teenager's father had been taken into custody and that there did not seem to be any link to the student protests that have swept across the country in recent weeks. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">de062bda-c61f-11f1-828c-2d5a86616301</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:43:38 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg">© Lou Benoist, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France 2022: The Choice</category><title>Battle for the French far right: Zemmour, Le Pen try to steal each other's thunder</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/france-2022-the-campaign/20220207-battle-for-the-far-right-zemmour-le-pen-fight-to-steal-each-other-s-thunder</link><description>
As France's April presidential election approaches, the campaign is getting under way in earnest. In this edition of our new show, we focus on the French Communist Party attempting a political comeback and discuss at length the battle raging between Eric Zemmour and Marine Le Pen for leadership of the French far right. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6ecf0724-8861-11ec-862b-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 07 Feb 2022 22:00:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Marc PERELMAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>Raphaël Glucksmann, the man who wants to be French president</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261011-a-profile-of-rapha%C3%ABl-glucksmann-the-man-who-wants-to-be-french-president</link><description>
Raphaël Glucksmann has won the primary to represent the French centre-left in the upcoming presidential elections, securing 66% of the vote. He now faces the challenge of building support for the centre-left in a political landscape where the far right, led by Marine Le Pen, remains a major force.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">99b61d02-c596-11f1-9bf5-777190d2ada5</guid><pubDate>Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:50:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fire destroys Paris's oldest covered food market</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-fire-burns-down-paris-s-oldest-covered-food-market</link><description>
A fire "completely destroyed" Paris's historic Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges early Monday, authorities said. The cause of the fire that swept through the capital's oldest covered food market remains unknown. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5504c60-c610-11f1-b48e-936bba59cf88</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:02:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg">© Creative Commons</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French police clash with teens blockading schools as unions stage day of protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-french-police-clash-with-teens-blockading-schools-as-union-stage-day-of-protests</link><description>
French teenagers on Tuesday clashed with police as they kept up a blockade of high schools in cities across the country to demand better conditions and more teacher hirings. The escalating standoff came as unions staged a day of demonstrations against a cost-cutting budget drafted by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's embattled government.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b23ed102-bbeb-11f1-861d-cf265369200f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:53:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Legion of Honour: Police investigate corruption claims for France’s top award</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-legion-of-honour-police-investigate-corruption-claims-for-france-s-top-award</link><description>
French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expensive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <description><p>Share price surges as chipmaker reverses decision to remove chief executive after US president ‘convinced’ its board</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/nils-pratley-on-finance/2026/nov/23/nvidia-board-jensen-huang-return">Comment: Nvidia’s humiliated board should resign out of embarrassment</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/jensen-huang-affair-timeline">Timeline: fall and comeback of Jensen Huang</a></p></li></ul><p>Nvidia has reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after Donald Trump directly intervened with the US AI chipmaker’s board of directors, in a stunning reversal of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns">the tech billionaire’s downfall</a>.</p><p>Speaking on Monday shortly after Nvidia’s surprise announcement that Huang had been restored to the top job – less than two weeks after he resigned – Trump said he had “convinced” the board to do it. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC.       <description><p>Despite the president’s attacks, Sea Services is training New England fishers in offshore wind construction and providing them with a second income stream</p><p>On a rainy September morning, the Pamela Ann, a rusty, 86ft (26-metre) scallop boat, docked in New Bedford, Massachusetts.       <description><p>Amid air chaos, travelers will have to navigate an outdated system (and complex company policies if it all goes wrong)</p><p>Millions of people are planning to fly in the US over the Thanksgiving holiday, just two weeks after the US Federal Aviation Administration’s 13 November <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/13/faa-ground-stop-flights-explained">ground stop</a> halted all flights nationwide for the first time since 9/11 (aside from a brief halt in 2023).</p><p>In the chaos that ensued, some travelers embarked on <a href="https://www.reddit.com/r/royalcaribbean/comments/1xvkopq/comment/19smxjywidlcw/?context=3">overnight drives</a> to catch cruise ships and <a href="https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/women-stranded-faa-ground-stop-buy-ford-bronco-27-hour-road-trip-rcna609629">bought new cars</a> to make business meetings. Many had to simply cancel their plans and incur the costs that came with it. More than 18,000 flights were cancelled at a potential cost to travelers of $1.9bn in lost time and related expenses, <a href="https://www.andersoneconomicgroup.com/analysis-nationwide-ground-stop-cost-travelers-nearly-2-billion/">Anderson Economic Group estimates</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global/2026/nov/23/thanksgiving-air-travel-us-explainer">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/24/crystal-palace-docked-three-points-wsl-extra-substitution-everton</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Too many substitutes used during win in opening game</p></li><li><p>They drop place to 13th but no extra points for Everton</p></li></ul><p>Crystal Palace have been deducted three points in the Women’s Super League after they made substitutions in four separate windows during their 1-0 victory over Everton in September.</p><p>Palace admitted breaching the competition’s rules and an independent tribunal ordered the points deduction, but no points will be awarded to Everton.       <description><p>Even without the charges, the Belgian maestro will be an unwelcome throwback to happier times for Enzo Maresca</p><p>As Manchester City come to terms with turbulence, one of their all-time greats has flown in to remind them of the best of times.       <title>Nwaneri at risk of becoming Arsenal’s forgotten teenager on return with Dortmund</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/24/ethan-nwaneri-arsenal-dortmund-mikel-arteta-champions-league</link>
      <description><p>Youngest player to appear in Premier League is struggling to establish himself on loan at the Bundesliga club</p><p>Ethan Nwaneri has one record Max Dowman can never break. It is more than four years since he became the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/sep/18/arsenals-ethan-nwaneri-becomes-youngest-premier-league-player-at-15">youngest player to appear in the Premier League</a>, with Dowman, his fellow Hale End academy graduate, older by 54 days when he made his <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/oct/30/max-dowman-journey-billericay-to-history-with-arsenal">highly anticipated debut</a>. But after a week when Arsenal published <a href="https://www.arsenal.com/news/max-dowmans-incredible-list-of-records-for-club-and-country-azbFG5M3BWVo">an article</a> dedicated to Dowman’s growing collection of milestones, Nwaneri risks becoming the club’s forgotten teenager.</p><p>Nwaneri joined Borussia Dortmund on loan in the summer and returns to the Emirates Stadium in the Champions League on Tuesday, although the 19-year-old will probably be on the bench, having not started for the German club yet in the competition. Despite making a good impression with an assist on his Bundesliga debut, against Hoffenheim, he has not started in the league since 17 October and has yet to complete more than 65 minutes in a Bundesliga match.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/24/ethan-nwaneri-arsenal-dortmund-mikel-arteta-champions-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Winger has not played for the USMNT since the World Cup and believes good club form is his route back into the squad</p><p>This was the USMNT’s summer. up for our free newsletter here</strong></a></p></li></ul><p>In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2025/oct/19/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">United’s victory at Anfield last season</a> was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter.</p><p>Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">lost only 4-0</a>. Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/mar/05/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023</a>. Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/mauricio-pochettino-can-now-see-just-how-desperate-manchester-united-are">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/gianni-infantino-world-cup-sell-off-plan-96-years-documents-payouts</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Management team were in line for huge payouts</p></li><li><p>Fifa denies Infantino would have profited from plan</p></li></ul><p>Gianni Infantino’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/aug/01/fifa-scraps-plan-to-sell-off-stakes-in-world-cup-after-widespread-backlash">failed Fifa Forward Enterprise plan</a> could have locked football in for up to 96 years while paying its management up to 5% of the scheme’s multibillion-pound value, according to documents seen by the Guardian.</p><p>Previously undisclosed communications by Fifa and Thrive Capital, the lead investor for the proposal, cast fresh light on the deal to sell off football’s crown jewels. They outline a plan, produced days before July’s final of the 2026 World Cup, to profit from the sport’s burgeoning commercial revenues for almost a century.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/gianni-infantino-world-cup-sell-off-plan-96-years-documents-payouts">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/nwsl-championship-washington-spirit-kansas-city-current</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Current’s opener came direct from a corner kick</p></li><li><p>Debinha, Trinity Rodman trade goals in stoppage time</p></li><li><p>Washington Spirit lose third consecutive NWSL final</p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2026/nov/21/washington-spirit-kansas-city-current-nwsl-championship-live-updates">Read Jeff Rueter’s minute-by-minute report</a></p></li></ul><p>It took five years, 90 minutes and a goal for the ages, but the Kansas City Current have their first-ever NWSL championship.</p><p>Riding a wave of momentum created by a 54th-minute <em>Olimpico</em> from midfielder Vanessa DiBernardo, and capping it off with an all-important breakaway winner from Debinha, the Current silenced the partisan, sellout crowd at the heavily-favored Washington Spirit’s home ground with a 2-1 victory on Saturday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/nwsl-championship-washington-spirit-kansas-city-current">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <guid>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/nwsl-championship-washington-spirit-kansas-city-current</guid>
      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/546fafdee8a7c55af0f3197c68e9e63455348a3f/311_0_4057_3247/master/4057.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=2208080e7b45fe3b49cc71f6ca1de2dc">

      </media:content>
      <media:content width="460" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/546fafdee8a7c55af0f3197c68e9e63455348a3f/311_0_4057_3247/master/4057.jpg?width=460&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=107a4c31ccce20f05e98cb40904c72c0">

      <title>‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p></p><p>Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.</p><p>It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/sevilla-real-betis-seville-derby-la-liga-kike-salas</link>
      <description><p>Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change</p><p>“If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, <em>this</em> was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ikiN2ah9DL4">Pelé against the Nazis</a>. Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears.</p><p>In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of <a href="https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37625798/sevilla-real-betis-laliga-best-rivalry-city-lives-sport">a city divided</a>, Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled <em>the </em>game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/23/sevilla-real-betis-seville-derby-la-liga-kike-salas">Continue reading...</a></description>

En 2025, en France, 111 femmes ont été tuées par leur conjoint ou ex-conjoint, laissant derrière elles des dizaines d'orphelins. Comment se relever après un tel drame ? Quel accompagnement pour aider ces enfants ? À la veille de la Journée de lutte contre les violences faites aux femmes, Natacha Vesnitch a rencontré Cloé et Eva-Louise. La première avait 7 ans quand elle a vu son père tuer sa mère en l'immolant. Eva-Louise, elle, avait 20 ans. Sa mère a été tuée d'une balle dans le thorax.  
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5b4bb494-e7f8-11f1-95ca-81da3ab2acbb/w:1024/p:16x9/cef-femicide.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5b4bb494-e7f8-11f1-95ca-81da3ab2acbb/w:1024/p:16x9/cef-femicide.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">55dbd094-e7fc-11f1-9282-5f4af93dbf06</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:43:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Natacha VESNITCH</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Cuisine : l'oeuf mayo, emblème du zinc français, a son nouveau champion du monde</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261124-cuisine-l-oeuf-mayo-embl%C3%A8me-du-zinc-fran%C3%A7ais-a-son-nouveau-champion-du-monde</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/294b8e80-e7f6-11f1-aed5-c131ae9bfe9c/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261124-111216-111407-CS-01.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/294b8e80-e7f6-11f1-aed5-c131ae9bfe9c/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261124-111216-111407-CS-01.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2edac2ee-e7f6-11f1-bf50-a1cd46abc08b</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:41:56 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Sports</category><title>CAN en direct : qui du Sénégal ou du Maroc sera déclaré champion ? Le verdict du TAS attendu</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/sports/20261124-can-en-direct-senegal-maroc-verdict-tas</link><description>
La finale de la CAN 2025 va enfin connaître son dénouement, mardi 24 novembre. Le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS) va rendre son verdict sur le litige opposant le Sénégal, vainqueur sur le terrain, et le Maroc, vainqueur sur tapis vert, et ainsi officialiser le nom du champion. Suivez notre direct, alors que l'Afrique retient son souffle.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/53ace694-e790-11f1-8226-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T083115Z-47471116-RC2TKOAJ8Y40-RTRMADP-3-NVIDIA-PROBE.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/53ace694-e790-11f1-8226-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T083115Z-47471116-RC2TKOAJ8Y40-RTRMADP-3-NVIDIA-PROBE.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1c2231b6-e790-11f1-8609-419bd98f53df</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 22:56:06 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/53ace694-e790-11f1-8226-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-10T083115Z-47471116-RC2TKOAJ8Y40-RTRMADP-3-NVIDIA-PROBE.jpg">© Suhaimi Abdullah, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Éco/Tech</category><title>Le chef de l'ONU espère voir d'ici un an un mécanisme pour limiter les risques posés par l'IA</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9co-tech/20261123-intelligence-artificielle-chef-onu-guterres-espere-voir-d-ici-un-an-mecanisme-pour-limiter-risques-ia</link><description>
Antonio Guterres a appelé lundi les États membres des Nations unies à élaborer, "d'ici l'année prochaine, un cadre multilatéral de gestion des risques liés à l'IA". Pour le chef de l'ONU, la première étape pourrait être de convenir de mesures de sécurité communes, d'un système d'évaluation et d'exigences minimales en matière de contrôle indépendant.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e51a5ede-dddd-11f1-ab12-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-11T095333Z-478881187-RC2LLOANGT8G-RTRMADP-3-CLIMATE-COP31.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e51a5ede-dddd-11f1-ab12-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-11T095333Z-478881187-RC2LLOANGT8G-RTRMADP-3-CLIMATE-COP31.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2dcd96d6-e78f-11f1-aba8-e124bf1f7616</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 22:42:46 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e51a5ede-dddd-11f1-ab12-29048b396e03/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-11T095333Z-478881187-RC2LLOANGT8G-RTRMADP-3-CLIMATE-COP31.jpg">© Murad Sezer, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Asie-Pacifique</category><title>Reconnaissance du génocide des Rohingya par la CIJ : 14 pays condamnent la Birmanie</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/asie-pacifique/20261123-birmanie-genocide-rohingya-14-pays-reconnaissent-decision-cij</link><description>
Le Royaume-Uni, l'Espagne, le Canada, l'Australie et dix autres pays ont affirmé lundi reconnaître la décision de la Cour internationale de justice, qui a reconnu la semaine dernière le génocide commis par la Birmanie contre les Rohingya. Ils exhortent la Birmanie à se "conformer pleinement à ses obligations en vertu du droit international, y compris à la décision de la Cour".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/88e681b0-e78d-11f1-9480-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324448432531.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/88e681b0-e78d-11f1-9480-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324448432531.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a3593998-e78d-11f1-8f6d-71728ab4ea1d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 22:31:48 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/88e681b0-e78d-11f1-9480-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324448432531.jpg">© Shamimul Islam Faisal, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

Dans un carnet intime et inédit dont des extraits ont été publiés mardi 24 novembre, le défunt pape François dit avoir vu le diable à trois reprises et une fois les « portes de l'enfer ».
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e61bf32-e7f2-11f1-b3eb-c131ae9bfe9c/w:1024/p:16x9/AP13061702721.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e61bf32-e7f2-11f1-b3eb-c131ae9bfe9c/w:1024/p:16x9/AP13061702721.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e7708026-e7f3-11f1-bda4-2f035de9e749</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:21:05 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/3e61bf32-e7f2-11f1-b3eb-c131ae9bfe9c/w:1024/p:16x9/AP13061702721.jpg">© AP/Alessandra Tarantino</source><dc:creator>RFI avec AFP</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Guerre en Ukraine: l'Union européenne propose d'interdire de compétition les athlètes russes sur son territoire</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261124-l-union-europ%C3%A9enne-propose-d-interdire-de-comp%C3%A9tition-les-athl%C3%A8tes-russes-sur-son-territoire</link><description>
Alors que les vingt-et-un « trains de sanctions » édictés par l'Union européenne contre la Russie depuis le déclenchement de la guerre en Ukraine en février 2022 ont touché les hydrocarbures, le secteur financier ou les armements, Bruxelles vient de franchir un nouveau cap dans sa volonté de faire plier le Kremlin en s'en prenant au sport et à la culture, deux valeurs centrales de la société civile. Des propositions qui pourraient toutefois avoir du mal à se concrétiser du fait qu'elles puissent être considérées comme une attaque directe contre les citoyens russes...
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/aea6cf2e-bde2-11f1-8dbb-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-18T010721Z-2125994934-RC2YYKASOKRW-RTRMADP-3-NEWZEALAND-EU.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/aea6cf2e-bde2-11f1-8dbb-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-18T010721Z-2125994934-RC2YYKASOKRW-RTRMADP-3-NEWZEALAND-EU.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4a1460cc-e7cb-11f1-87d4-9fbe8f526646</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 06:29:46 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/aea6cf2e-bde2-11f1-8dbb-69fad0a7cb9f/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-09-18T010721Z-2125994934-RC2YYKASOKRW-RTRMADP-3-NEWZEALAND-EU.jpg">© Reuters/Yves Herman </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Accents d'Europe</category><title>Dix ans après le référendum sur le Brexit... le Bregret?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/accents-d-europe/20261123-dix-ans-apr%C3%A8s-le-r%C3%A9f%C3%A9rendum-sur-le-brexit-le-bregret</link><description>
Dix ans après le référendum sur le Brexit qui a présidé au départ effectif du Royaume-Uni de l’Europe... Londres opère lentement, mais sûrement un rapprochement avec le continent. Le Brexit a causé plus de mal que de bien, a résumé le nouveau Premier ministre travailliste Andy Burnham, qui n’exclut pas un retour de son pays dans l’UE. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8bfc34f0-e45c-11f1-8d7f-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26322414753525.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8bfc34f0-e45c-11f1-8d7f-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26322414753525.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">96183ba6-e762-11f1-a96c-7b5726cadb9b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 20:05:25 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Frédérique Lebel</dc:creator></item><item><category>La fabrique du monde</category><title>Pedro Sanchez peut-il réussir sa «remontada» et rester au pouvoir?</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/la-fabrique-du-monde/20261123-pedro-sanchez-peut-il-r%C3%A9ussir-sa-remontada-et-rester-au-pouvoir</link><description>
Dernière ligne droite avant les élections législatives anticipées qui auront lieu ce dimanche 29 novembre en Espagne. Le scrutin s’annonce périlleux pour Pedro Sanchez, donné perdant dans les sondages. Spécialiste des « remontadas » spectaculaires, le chef du gouvernement socialiste pourra-t-il néanmoins faire mentir les sondages et rester aux affaires ?  
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2e20faec-c08e-11f1-8911-dd51fcab6130/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C9RY9EA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/2e20faec-c08e-11f1-8911-dd51fcab6130/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C9RY9EA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">14896756-e724-11f1-90c6-8324eea7e277</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:20:09 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Daniel Vallot</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Belgique: journée de grève nationale contre la vie chère, le trafic aérien entièrement paralysé</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261123-belgique-journ%C3%A9e-de-gr%C3%A8ve-nationale-contre-la-vie-ch%C3%A8re-le-trafic-a%C3%A9rien-enti%C3%A8rement-paralys%C3%A9</link><description>
Il n'y aura pas d'avion dans le ciel belge ce lundi 23 novembre : c'est la conséquence d'une grève nationale contre la vie chère. Alors que le gouvernement fédéral belge cherche difficilement à négocier un budget de rigueur qui vise à économiser 10 milliards d'euros au cours des prochaines années, les syndicats ont appelé à faire front commun et à une « grande mobilisation citoyenne » pour dénoncer la politique d’austérité ainsi que la baisse du pouvoir d’achat. Une journée à laquelle ont décidé de se joindre les contrôleurs aériens, ce qui va entièrement paralyser le trafic des avions toute la journée. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/30485b52-1aa4-11f1-a9dc-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25330424076154.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/30485b52-1aa4-11f1-a9dc-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25330424076154.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2b34cece-e719-11f1-9a3f-47fc1c531e42</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:00:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/30485b52-1aa4-11f1-a9dc-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25330424076154.jpg">© Mark Carlson / AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Hongrie: la détention provisoire d'un ancien ministre d'Orban dans une enquête de corruption prolongée</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261123-hongrie-la-d%C3%A9tention-provisoire-d-un-ancien-ministre-d-orban-dans-une-enqu%C3%AAte-de-corruption-prolong%C3%A9e</link><description>
En Hongrie, Miklos Sesztak, l’ancien ministre du Développement national entre 2014 et 2018, et actuel député au Parlement hongrois, a été arrêté fin septembre. Il est soupçonné d’avoir détourné de l’argent public et d’avoir touché d’énormes pots-de-vin. Lors d’une perquisition à son domicile, la police a trouvé plusieurs coffres-forts vides. Il y a huit jours, les autorités hongroises découvraient un immense butin : près de 16 millions d’euros en liquide, cachés dans des forêts, des granges et des entrepôts. La détention provisoire de Miklos Sesztak a été prolongée jusqu’à fin janvier.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ec5628ba-dfe4-11f0-9eaa-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25351567398088.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ec5628ba-dfe4-11f0-9eaa-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25351567398088.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0120195e-e511-11f1-9083-078c74fc6df3</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:36:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/ec5628ba-dfe4-11f0-9eaa-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/AP25351567398088.jpg">© AP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Contre la guerre, pour la jeunesse: vague de manifestations à travers l'Europe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-contre-la-guerre-pour-la-jeunesse-vague-de-manifestations-%C3%A0-travers-l-europe</link><description>
Contre la « militarisation » de la société et la vie chère, pour l'avenir des jeunes, l'éducation, le droit au logement, le climat : des dizaines de milliers de manifestants se mobilisent à travers l'Europe vendredi 20 novembre, sur fond de rejet des institutions. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1853515c-e50e-11f1-8321-3bce4db5bc5f</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 18:25:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/c4918b74-e50d-11f1-94fe-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/GettyImages-2306076594.jpg">© Massimiliano Donati / Getty Images</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>Le Danemark accuse la Russie d'avoir tenté d'assassiner un rappeur ukrainien</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-le-danemark-va-expulser-un-diplomate-russe-apr%C3%A8s-la-tentative-d-assassinat-d-un-ukrainien-sur-son-sol</link><description>
Le Danemark va expulser l'attaché de défense de l'ambassade de Russie après la tentative d'assassinat d'un rappeur ukrainien sur son sol, qu'il soupçonne Moscou d'avoir orchestré, a indiqué vendredi 20 novembre le ministre danois des Affaires étrangères. La diplomatie russe a promis de riposter. « Moscou donnera une réponse appropriée », a indiqué la porte-parole du ministère russe des Affaires étrangères, Maria Zakharova, citée par l'agence de presse TASS.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7863937e-e507-11f1-99b0-bbfd8e7adaf9</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:35:50 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/449d07e6-e507-11f1-8364-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86T2RT.jpg">AFP - EMIL HELMS</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>Invité international</category><title>Manifestations en Europe: «Une volonté de converger au niveau transnational et avec d'autres générations»</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/podcasts/invit%C3%A9-international/20261120-manifestations-en-europe-une-volont%C3%A9-de-converger-au-niveau-transnational-et-avec-d-autres-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9rations</link><description>
La mobilisation contre la vie chère traverse toute l'Europe : des millions de personnes sont attendues dans les rues contre la vie chère et pour le droit au logement. Ce mouvement de fond, lancé à partir de ce vendredi 20 novembre, traduit des réalités communes. Ces luttes peuvent-elles vraiment converger ? Quels modes d'action pour quelles revendications ? L’analyse du sociologue Paolo Stuppia, enseignant à Sciences Po Paris et co-auteur de Géopolitique de la jeunesse – Engagement et (dé)mobilisations, publiée aux éditions Cavalier bleu.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9142dd72-e4f9-11f1-8056-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324446135271.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9142dd72-e4f9-11f1-8056-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324446135271.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a69a8ac8-e4f2-11f1-a69d-dfb7bbed3c72</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:07:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Candice Mazaud-Tomazic</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>À la Une: Aleksandar Čupić, le sage à la tête du Parlement serbe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-%C3%A0-la-une-aleksandar-%C4%8Dupi%C4%87-le-sage-%C3%A0-la-t%C3%AAte-du-parlement-serbe</link><description>
Une revue de presse des Balkans en partenariat avec Le Courrier des Balkans.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eb8a088e-e4f2-11f1-8ab1-dffd4ffb6f91</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:41:30 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/a7f28112-e4f4-11f1-85e4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T152302Z-275612966-RC22ROAP2GDQ-RTRMADP-3-SERBIA-PARLIAMENT.jpg">© Djordje Kojadinovic / Reuters</source><dc:creator>Courrier des Balkans</dc:creator></item><item><category>Europe</category><title>UE/Royaume-Uni: Andy Burnham annonce une «réflexion» en 2027 sur les relations à long terme</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/fr/europe/20261120-ue-royaume-uni-andy-burnham-annonce-une-r%C3%A9flexion-en-2027-sur-les-relations-%C3%A0-long-terme</link><description>
Pour son premier sommet avec l’UE, le Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham peut s’estimer satisfait. Européens et Britanniques se sont mis d’accord sur trois dossiers concernant les jeunes, les émissions de CO2 et les normes alimentaires. La « remise à zéro » imaginée par son prédécesseur Keir Starmer pour les relations entre Londres et Bruxelles est désormais sur des rails, même si union douanière, libre-circulation et marché unique restent des lignes rouges pour les Britanniques. Les Européens affirment avoir tourné la page du Brexit et se satisfont ouvertement des accords ponctuels comme ceux qui ont été trouvés ce vendredi 20 novembre.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f35856f6-e4f2-11f1-85c2-81e9611d4583</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:30:12 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/cfd3cb76-e4f1-11f1-a528-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324496448442.jpg">AP Photo/Marius Burgelman - Marius Burgelman</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

            <description><![CDATA[De jeunes pêcheurs de Yenne Todd, âgés de 18 à 22 ans, ne cachent ni leur désarroi ni leur envie de partir. En 2025, en France, 111 femmes ont été tuées par leur conjoint ou ex-conjoint, laissant derrière elles des dizaines d'orphelins. Comment se relever après un tel drame ? Quel accompagnement pour aider ces enfants ? À la veille de la Journée de lutte contre les violences faites aux femmes, Natacha Vesnitch a rencontré Cloé et Eva-Louise. La première avait 7 ans quand elle a vu son père tuer sa mère en l'immolant. Eva-Louise, elle, avait 20 ans. Sa mère a été tuée d'une balle dans le thorax.  
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5b4bb494-e7f8-11f1-95ca-81da3ab2acbb/w:1024/p:16x9/cef-femicide.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5b4bb494-e7f8-11f1-95ca-81da3ab2acbb/w:1024/p:16x9/cef-femicide.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">55dbd094-e7fc-11f1-9282-5f4af93dbf06</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 11:43:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Natacha VESNITCH</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Mort de Nahel Merzouk : la justice ordonne un procès pour meurtre à l'encontre du policier</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261124-mort-nahel-merzouk-justice-ordonne-proc%C3%A8s-pour-meurtre-policier</link><description>
Trois ans après l'homicide de Nahel Merzouk, 17 ans, tué à bout portant par un tir de policier à la suite d'un refus d'obtempérer, la cour d'appel de Versailles a ordonné un procès pour meurtre à l'encontre du policier responsable de la mort du jeune homme dans cette affaire qui avait provoqué des nuits d'émeutes en France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/401d335e-e7e0-11f1-b649-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D84V2NQ.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/401d335e-e7e0-11f1-b649-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D84V2NQ.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c802ce5a-e7e0-11f1-9eaf-03e929159d16</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:27:33 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/401d335e-e7e0-11f1-b649-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D84V2NQ.jpg">© Zakaria Abdelkalfi, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Ouverture du Congrès des maires sur fond de bataille pour l'Élysée</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261124-ouverture-du-congr%C3%A8s-des-maires-sur-fond-de-bataille-pour-l-%C3%A9lys%C3%A9e</link><description>
La puissante Association des maires de France (AMF) se réunit du 24 au 26 novembre à Paris, où les candidats à l'élection présidentielle vont se presser, en particulier ceux en quête des 500 parrainages nécessaires à leur candidature. Mais ce rendez-vous annuel sera surtout marqué par l'élection de son président. Déjà candidat à la présidentielle, David Lisnard espère également renouveler son mandat à la tête de l'AMF.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c2b48f5e-bc27-11f1-bec4-852b23529bb9/w:1024/p:16x9/baf2d6747af2daa0eeaa6ede28eb836708717521.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c2b48f5e-bc27-11f1-bec4-852b23529bb9/w:1024/p:16x9/baf2d6747af2daa0eeaa6ede28eb836708717521.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">e4ffbbd0-e79a-11f1-945f-0f17a4d04297</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 00:06:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c2b48f5e-bc27-11f1-bec4-852b23529bb9/w:1024/p:16x9/baf2d6747af2daa0eeaa6ede28eb836708717521.jpg">© Sébastien Bozon, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Terres rares : Emmanuel Macron annonce que la France va se doter de "stocks stratégiques"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261123-terres-rares-macron-annonce-france-doter-stocks-strat%C3%A9giques</link><description>
Emmanuel Macron a annoncé un projet pour pourvoir la France de "stocks stratégiques" de minerais critiques, a déclaré l'Élysée lundi. Le programme inspiré des réserves stratégiques de pétrole aura pour but de sécuriser l'approvisionnement en terres rares et en "certains métaux prioritaires" et de réduire la dépendance vis-à-vis de la Chine.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e0bb6456-e782-11f1-b064-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86Z2CF.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e0bb6456-e782-11f1-b064-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86Z2CF.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">193af01c-e77e-11f1-a7de-f11b92b1705d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 23 Nov 2026 21:06:36 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/e0bb6456-e782-11f1-b064-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D86Z2CF.jpg">© Aurélien Morissard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Le débat</category><title>Présidentielle 2027 : qui pourra rassembler ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/le-d%C3%A9bat/20261123-pr%C3%A9sidentielle-qui-pourra-rassembler</link><description>
À moins de cinq mois du premier tour de la présidentielle, prévu le 18 avril, la course à l’Élysée s’annonce particulièrement disputée. Dernier en date à entrer dans la course : Dominique de Villepin. Plusieurs candidats de la droite et du centre veulent s’affronter dans une primaire afin de désigner un seul représentant, mais l’idée ne fait pas l’unanimité. David Lisnard, qui est en progression dans les sondages, entend peser dans les discussions et pose ses conditions.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ec88460c-e514-11f1-8bce-43bc8e8d3f8d</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 19:02:24 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg">© Geoffroy van der Hasselt, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fuites au ministère de l'Intérieur : comment le RN a progressivement séduit les hauts fonctionnaires</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-fuites-au-minist%C3%A8re-de-l-int%C3%A9rieur-comment-le-rn-a-progressivement-s%C3%A9duit-les-hauts-fonctionnaires</link><description>
